[[Mangalore University]] | occupation = Businessman | title = Chairman & MD, [[Café Coffee Day]] | boards = [[Mindtree]] }} {{Indian name|Siddhartha Hegde or Siddhartha|Veerappa Gangaiah}}'''Veerappa Gangaiah Siddhartha Hegde''' ({{Birth based on age at death|60|2019|7|29}} – 29 July 2019) was an Indian businessman from [[Karnataka]].{{cite web|url=http://mybtechlife.com/the-list-of-great-entrepreneurs-in-india-2015/|title=The List of Great Entrepreneurs of India in 2015|publisher=MyBTechLife|author=Srikar Muthyala|date=29 September 2015|access-date=7 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114000446/http://mybtechlife.com/the-list-of-great-entrepreneurs-in-india-2015/|archive-date=14 January 2016|url-status=dead}} He was the founder of the cafe chain [[Café Coffee Day]] and was its chairman and managing director. He was on the board of directors of [[Mindtree]], GTV, Liqwid Krystal, Way2wealth Brokers, Coffee Day Natural Resources, and Way2wealth Securities. After going missing on the evening of 29 July 2019, his body was found by three fishermen at the [[Hoige Bazaar]] beach, near the mouth of the river [[Netravati River|Nethravati]] on 31 July.{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/cafe-cofee-day-owner-vg-siddharthas-body-found-from-netravati-river/articleshow/70458460.cms|title=Cafe Coffee Day owner VG Siddhartha dead, body found|date=2019-07-31|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2019-08-03}} == Early life == Veerappa Gangaiah Siddhartha Hegde was born to Gangaiah Hegde in the [[Malenadu]] region of [[Chikmagalur district]] in [[Karnataka]].{{cite news |title='Coffee king' and more |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/coffee-king-and-more/story-uwIzBLvzaw3UXvbLNNh2hM.html |access-date=3 August 2019 |work=Hindustan Times |date=1 August 2019 |language=en}} He hailed from a very affluent family of coffee planters belonging to the [[Vokkaliga]] community.{{Cite news|date=2019-08-27|title=A month after VG Siddhartha's demise, CCD founder's father passes away|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/a-month-after-vg-siddharthas-demise-ccd-founders-father-passes-away/articleshow/70836030.cms|access-date=2020-06-24}} He received a master's degree in economics from [[St. Aloysius College, Mangalore|St. Aloysius College]] and [[Mangalore University]], Karnataka.{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mangaluru/Rural-youth-have-greater-killer-instinct-avers-Cafe-Coffee-Day-chief-V-G-Siddhartha/articleshow/54276737.cms|title=Rural youth|access-date=30 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160912062808/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mangaluru/Rural-youth-have-greater-killer-instinct-avers-Cafe-Coffee-Day-chief-V-G-Siddhartha/articleshow/54276737.cms|archive-date=12 September 2016|url-status=live|publisher=Times of India}} == Career == At the age of 24, he joined J M Financial Limited in 1983–1984 in [[Mumbai]] as a management trainee/intern in portfolio management and securities trading on the Indian stock market. After two years, he returned to Bangalore. With capital given by his father, Siddhartha bought stocks worth ₹30,000 and started the company Sivan Securities. In 1999, it was renamed Way2wealth Securities Ltd. Its venture capital division came to be known as Global Technology Ventures (GTV). He established his coffee trading company ABC in Karnataka 1993, with a ₹6 crore turnover. He bought an ailing coffee curing unit in [[Hassan, India|Hassan]] for ₹4 crore and improved it. The company now has the largest curing capacity in India at 75,000 tonnes.{{cite web|url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2000/jul/03sidart.htm|title=Rediff On The NeT Business Special: V G Siddhartha: From coffee to cyber cafes|access-date=3 September 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091103045924/http://www.rediff.com/money/2000/jul/03sidart.htm|archive-date=3 November 2009|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=http://business.in.com/article/big-bet/vg-siddhartha-is-branching-out/26282/0|title=V.G. Siddhartha is Branching Out|work=Forbes India|access-date=9 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008092739/http://business.in.com/article/big-bet/vg-siddhartha-is-branching-out/26282/0|archive-date=8 October 2011|url-status=dead}} He was the first entrepreneur in Karnataka to set up a café in 1996 ([[Café Coffee Day]], a chain of "youth hangout" coffee parlors). By 2018, the chain had over 1700 cafés in India.{{Cite web |url=http://www.coffeeday.com/PDF/Coffee_Day_Annual_report_2018.pdf |title=Coffee Day Annual Report 2018 |page=13 |access-date=24 July 2019 }} His cafes attract 40,000 to 50,000 visitors a week. Siddhartha also held board seats in GTV, [[Mindtree]], Liqwid Krystal, Way2Wealth, and Ittiam. In 2000, he founded Global Technology Ventures Ltd, a company that identifies, invests in, and mentors Indian companies engaged in technologies.{{cite web|url=http://www.way2wealth.com/group_companies.asp|title=Way2Wealth Brokers Pvt. Ltd.|access-date=15 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110701005447/http://www.way2wealth.com/group_companies.asp|archive-date=1 July 2011|url-status=dead}} GTV set up [[Global Village Tech Park]] on a {{convert|59|acre|m2|adj=on}} plot as an incubator park in Bangalore, providing office space, communication links, recreational facilities, and a commercial centre. In 1999, GTV was valued by BankAm at $100 million. He planted banana trees on 3,000 acres (1,214 ha) and had plans to export bananas. The Dark Forest Furniture Company is named after V. G. Siddhartha's Kathale Kaad (Dark Forest in Kannada) estate in [[Chikmagalur]].{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Coffee-king-on-Amazon-trail-for-furniture-biz/articleshow/7907883.cms|title=Coffee king on Amazon trail for furniture biz|work=The Times of India|date=8 April 2011 |access-date=4 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160624163942/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Coffee-king-on-Amazon-trail-for-furniture-biz/articleshow/7907883.cms|archive-date=24 June 2016|url-status=live}} Sical Logistics Ltd, a logistics company founded in India in 1955, was acquired by Coffee Day group in 2011.{{cite news |title=VG Siddhartha and Cafe Coffee Day: A timeline of highlights |url=http://www.forbesindia.com/article/special/vg-siddhartha-and-cafe-coffee-day-a-timeline-of-highlights/54573/1 |access-date=31 July 2019 |work=Forbes India |language=en}} On 21 September 2017, a tax raid was conducted at more than 20 of V. G. Siddhartha's locations in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, and Chikmagalur by senior officers of the Income Tax Department of Karnataka and Goa regions.{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/it-raids-offices-owned-by-v-g-sidhartha-son-in-law-of-s-m-krishna/articleshow/60775062.cms|title=I-T raids son-in-law of former Karnataka CM SM Krishna, owner of Cafe Coffee Day chain|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=21 September 2017 |access-date=21 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922095037/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/it-raids-offices-owned-by-v-g-sidhartha-son-in-law-of-s-m-krishna/articleshow/60775062.cms|archive-date=22 September 2017|url-status=live}} == Personal life == Siddhartha was married to Malavika Krishna{{Cite web |date=August 9, 2024 |title=Malavika Hegde Life Story: How she became the CEO of Coffee Day Group? |url=https://www.newshour.press/business/malavika-hegde-life-story-how-she-became-the-ceo-of-coffee-day-group/ |website=NewsHour}} and had two children Amartya Hegde and Ishaan Hegde.{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesnownews.com/mirror-now/in-focus/article/vg-siddhartha-family-all-you-need-to-know-about-ccd-owners-family-tree/461058|title=CCD founder VG Siddhartha family tree: From father-in-law SM Krishna to wife Malavika Krishna and sons|website=www.timesnownews.com|date=31 July 2019 |language=en-GB|access-date=2019-07-31}}{{Cite web|date=2019-07-31|title=Coffee King laid to rest|url=https://www.deccanherald.com/state/top-karnataka-stories/coffee-king-laid-to-rest-751133.html|access-date=2020-06-24|website=Deccan Herald|language=en}} His son Amartya married to [[D. K. Shivakumar|D. K. Shivakumar's]] daughter Aishwarya Shivakumar on 14 February 2021.{{Cite web|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/karnataka/2021/feb/08/vvips-from-delhi-to-land-in-bengaluru-for-wedding-of-dk-shivakumars-daughter-2261012.html|title=VVIPs from Delhi to land in Bengaluru for wedding of DK Shivakumar's daughter|date=8 February 2021 }} Siddhartha was the son-in-law of [[S. M. Krishna]], the [[Chief Minister of Karnataka]], [[Minister of External Affairs (India)|Indian Minister for External Affairs]] and [[Governors of Maharashtra|Governor of Maharashtra]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/body-of-cafe-coffee-day-owner-vg-siddhartha-found-says-deputy-commissioner/article28766299.ece|title=Body of Café Coffee Day owner V.G. Siddhartha found|date=2019-07-31|work=The Hindu|access-date=2019-07-31|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X}} ==Death== On the evening of 29 July 2019, he told his driver to stop as they approached the bridge over the [[Netravati River|Nethravati River]] in [[Ullal]], [[Mangalore]]. He directed the driver to wait for him at the other end of the bridge giving an impression that he wanted to take a stroll. The driver reported to the police that he did not show up even after an hour; which led to a search of the area for him. The [[Indian Coast Guard]] and [[National Disaster Response Force]] eventually joined a search.{{cite news|url=https://www.news18.com/news/india/vg-siddhartha-missing-lsex-coffee-day-founder-sm-krishnas-son-in-law-untraceable-cops-launch-probe-mangaluru-karnataka-2250903.html|title=VG Siddhartha Missing|publisher=News18|access-date=30 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190730083913/https://www.news18.com/news/india/vg-siddhartha-missing-live-cafe-coffee-day-founder-sm-krishnas-son-in-law-untraceable-cops-launch-probe-mangaluru-karnataka-2250903.html|archive-date=30 July 2019|url-status=live}} A [[suicide note|letter]],{{Cite news|last1=Rajput|first1=Rashmi|last2=Krishnan|first2=Raghu|date=2019-07-31|title=I-T says VG Siddhartha's signature on note not matching|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/tax-department-acted-as-per-law-in-ccd-promoter-siddhartha-case-sources/articleshow/70449827.cms?from=mdr|access-date=2020-06-24}} apparently written by Siddhartha and addressed to his company board, shareholders, and family, surfaced a few hours after he went missing.{{cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/cafe-coffee-day-owner-vg-siddhartha-missing-letter-ccd-board-1575061-2019-07-30|title=I give up: CCD owner VG Siddhartha goes missing, leaves distressing letter for board|publisher=India Today|access-date=30 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190730094325/https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/cafe-coffee-day-owner-vg-siddhartha-missing-letter-ccd-board-1575061-2019-07-30|archive-date=30 July 2019|url-status=live}} This letter detailed the unbearable pressure he was subjected to over the years and the harassment he faced under the "previous" Director General of Income Tax (Investigation) (referred to as DG in the letter). His body was found at the [[Hoige Bazaar]] beach on 31 July around 6:30 am by local fishermen who informed the police.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/cafe-coffee-day-founder-vg-siddharthas-body-found-two-days-after-he-went-missing-2077873|title=Cafe Coffee Day Founder's Body Found 2 Days After He Went Missing|website=NDTV.com|access-date=2019-07-31}} His body was cremated at Chethanahalli coffee estate owned by his family in [[Chikmagalur district|Chikkamagalur]] district on 31 July 2019.{{cite news |title=VG Siddhartha cremated in Chethanahalli coffee estate |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/vg-siddhartha-cremated-in-chethanahalli-coffee-estate/articleshow/70470211.cms |access-date=1 August 2019 |work=The Economic Times |date=31 July 2019}} A police investigation into his death, reported suicide by drowning as the cause.{{cite news |title=V.G. Siddhartha's death: final report confirms it is suicide |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/vg-siddharthas-death-final-report-confirms-it-is-suicide/article29259250.ece |access-date=26 August 2019 |work=The Hindu |date=26 August 2019 |language=en-IN}} ==Awards== *"Entrepreneur of the Year" for 2002–03 by ''[[The Economic Times]]''{{cite web |title=V.G. Veerappa Gangaiah Siddhartha Hegde (1958 or 1959 – 29 July 2019) was an Indian businessman from Karnataka. He was the founder of the cafe chain Café Coffee Day and was its chairman and managing director. He was on the board of directors of Mindtree, GTV, Liqwid Krystal, Way2wealth Brokers, Coffee Day Natural Resources, and Way2wealth Securities.
After going missing on the evening of 29 July 2019, his body was found by three fishermen at the Hoige Bazaar beach, near the mouth of the river Nethravati on 31 July.
